findings.summary: The bars are drawn on a logarithmic x axis, so bar length is not proportional to value: the 7.6 ms booking bar renders nearly as long as the 21.4 ms bar and about three quarters the 107.8 ms topology read, though it is fourteen times smaller. A reader comparing lengths misranks the stages, and only the printed values correct it; a dot or lollipop mark would encode the ratios the text relies on.

The value labels and the target annotation are drawn at 11 pt while the data-ink style sheet the script loads sets 14 pt for direct labels, so this figure's numbers render smaller than the same 14 pt tick labels beside them and smaller than other figures on the page. Readable, but below the size the repository's figure rules specify and inconsistent within one canvas.

The grey bar mixes quantities on one axis: 'map, width 16 per slice' is 21.4 ms per solve at batch width 16, not a stage of one step, while the axis label reads 'wall per stage [ms]'. The bar's own series label and the caption disambiguate it, so the defect is the axis label's silence rather than a lost distinction.

item_verdicts.contrast: pass — near-black category labels and values on white, and the red target label clears the white ground comfortably; the grey width-16 bar reads as data rather than fading out.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass — six solid bars plus one-line value labels carry the ink; no gridlines, no fills, no shading, no legend box.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass — white ground, top and right spines removed; the only non-data mark is a 1 ms threshold drawn 1.2 pt dotted in red, which the caption identifies as the target.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass — no text is clipped or overlapping: category labels sit left of the axis, each value sits in clear space right of its bar end, and the '1 ms target' annotation sits above the top bar rather than on it.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass — on the 1400 x 720 px render every category label, bar and printed value reads at a glance, from the 735.7 ms Jacobian bar down to the 6.4 ms linear solve, without zoom. The log-axis length distortion noted in the findings does not stop a reader reading the figure, because every value is printed and the caption and text give the percentages.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass — the figure's message is distance from a threshold, which is spatial rather than tabular; the same numbers also sit in the table above it in the evidence fragment, but the figure is not depicting a table's content.
